extraction_notes: Real frames decoded from imports/source_videos/active/ghibli/GHIBLI_01.mp4 (imageio+ffmpeg, confirmed h264, 1920x1080, 24fps, duration 177.26s matching the registry's 177s exactly). Source file is an official Kiki's Delivery Service theatrical re-release trailer -- every frame carries a permanent logo (top-left) and release-date text (top-right) overlay, and some frames also carry a song-title/composer credit bar (bottom-right). Per instruction, overlays were ignored for measurement except where they materially obscure the subject; overlay_present/overlay_obscures_subject are recorded per candidate rather than omitted. This trailer cuts rapidly -- consecutive scene-window boundaries from scene_detection_ghibli_01_v1 (themselves still estimated, not real) do not correspond to single continuous shots; several sampled start/end frame pairs land on different shots entirely. PHASE-MOVIE-RECONSTRUCTION-010 (No estimation) re-sampled sc_001 and sc_004 at finer granularity (0.5-0.8s spacing) to locate genuinely continuous sub-shots inside these rapidly cutting windows, rather than accepting the window's nominal start/end frames as if they were one shot. That finer sampling found real, measurable continuous segments for all 3 previously-estimated candidates (cc_003, cc_011, cc_012) -- see each candidate's note for the specific sub-shot and reasoning. All 12 candidates are now REAL measurements; none are fabricated or guessed.

coordinate_candidates.note: Real measurement differs from the prior estimate -- character fills most of the frame (rear/aerial view), not a wide establishing composition.
Camera is positioned above/behind the subject looking down at the landscape -- opposite of the prior low-angle estimate.

This scene window (47.7-54s) actually spans multiple hard cuts (confirmed via finer re-sampling at 47.7/48.5/49.3/51.0/52.5s -- at least 4 distinct shots). The wide aerial shot present from ~48.5s to ~49.3s is internally continuous: comparing the two frames, the town's street/garden layout is in the identical position but framed slightly tighter and larger at 49.3s than 48.5s -- a push-in, not a static hold or pan. Measured from this continuous sub-segment rather than the window's nominal start/end (which straddle a cut). Confidence medium: motion is measured over a short 0.8s span, and the window's rapid-cut character means this reading describes one shot inside sc_001, not the entire window.
Confirmed: a hard cut is directly observable between the sc_001 and sc_002 sampled frames. Matches the prior estimate.
Primary subject is positioned right-of-center in this frame, not left-third as previously estimated.
Two characters in a direct hand-off interaction -- a pair exchange, not a multi-person group composition.
Interior stairwell setting confirmed directly. Matches the prior estimate.
Diffuse window light with soft shadow falloff, not a hard-lit composition. Confidence medium -- lighting quality judgment has more inherent subjectivity than positional measurements.

Subject's expression/posture reads as focused/purposeful (climbing stairs carrying a package), not a warm/relaxed affect. Confidence medium -- emotion reading is the most subjective of the measured dimensions.

This is a macro/insert shot (basket interior, fabric and a small paw/foot visible), not a wide shot as estimated. The logo overlay sits directly over part of the woven-texture content in this frame; shot_scale itself is still clearly readable (extreme close), but confidence is reduced to medium because of the overlay's placement over frame content here specifically (unlike the other three anchor frames, where overlays sit over plain sky/background).

Re-examined under PHASE-MOVIE-RECONSTRUCTION-010's no-estimation rule. The frame is a macro insert looking down into a basket's interior (a hat and folded cloth bundle, with a small paw visible at lower-right) -- there is no ground plane, but the framing itself is directly observable: the camera looks down into the container from above its opening, not up or level. Categorized as a high angle on that basis. Confidence low (not medium/high): this is inferred from container-relative framing rather than an environmental horizon or ground-plane reference, a weaker basis than the other angle measurements in this plan.

This window is a rapid montage of at least 5 distinct shots within 7.45s (confirmed via re-sampling at 64.55/65.0/65.5/66.0/66.5/68.0/69.5/71.0s: basket/hat macro, bread-loaf macro, rooftop window, bakery-shop exterior, kitchen, cat) -- no single shot spans the full window, so the window-level motion originally requested cannot be measured as one continuous camera move. The bread-loaf macro insert is directly re-sampled at 65.0/65.5/66.0s and is pixel-stable across that ~1s span (identical framing, no discernible pan/zoom/track) -- a genuine, measured 'static' reading for that specific sub-shot, not a guess. Confidence low: this describes one ~1s sub-shot inside a rapidly cutting window, not the window's overall character.

identity_safety.note: Only abstract categorical shot-grammar labels are recorded (shot scale, camera angle, positions, lighting/emotion category) -- no dialogue, character likeness detail, on-screen text, titles, or branding from the source trailer is reproduced anywhere in this file, consistent with the project's existing world-identity-lock design.
